title: Viva Engage: advanced moderation permission for corporate communicators
summary: The permission's default, licensing conditions, administrative paths and automation are supported by Microsoft documentation. The checklist names theme management and historical-conversation retrieval without corresponding controls-table rows; these are minor completeness findings.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans advanced moderation access control for corporate communicators in Viva Engage.
claims.quote: Network admins can choose to enable advanced moderation access for corporate communicators to manage AI themes + keywords detected within organization.

claims.claim: The advanced moderation permission is off until an administrator assigns it, corresponding to admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: The advanced moderation permission is OFF by default. Verified Admins, Network Admins, and Engage Admins can assign the advanced moderation permission to corporate communicator accounts.

claims.claim: Permission management is reached in Viva Engage admin center through Setup & Configuration > Admin Roles.
claims.quote:
1. Go to the Viva Engage Admin Center.
2. Open Setup & Configuration.
3. Select Admin Roles.

claims.claim: No automation for assigning the separate advanced moderation permission is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage advanced moderation granular permission Microsoft Graph PowerShell API; graph/api advanced moderation permission engagementRoleMember beta. Opened engagement-api-overview, engagementrolemember and engagementrole-post-members: role membership only, no moderation permission property.

claims.claim: Corporate Communicator assignment uses Viva Engage admin center > Setup and configuration > Admin roles > Corporate communicator > Add user.
claims.quote: In the Viva Engage admin center, on the Setup and configuration tab, select Admin roles. Select the Corporate communicator tab > Add user to search for a user by name or email ID.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/employeeExperience/roles/{engagementRoleId}/members assigns a Viva Engage role to a user.
claims.quote:
Create a new engagementRoleMember object that assigns a Viva Engage role to a user.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/employeeExperience/roles/a40473a5-0fb4-a250-e029-f6fe33d07733/members

claims.claim: AI settings are reached in Viva Engage admin center through Setup & configuration > Manage analytics > Analytics settings > Feature access management.
claims.quote:
Select the Setup & configuration tab, and select Manage analytics.
Activate AI-related features from the Analytics settings page > Feature access management.

claims.claim: The printed Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy call uses valid Exchange Online parameters to disable the selected feature for everyone.
claims.quote:
Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone
The FeatureId value is returned in the output of the cmdlet.

claims.quote: Theme moderation requires at least 50% of users in your organization to have the Viva Suite license, or the Viva Employee Communications and Communities license.

claims.claim: Keyword monitoring, detected conversations and the advanced moderation destination are included in the Microsoft 365 enterprise plan.
claims.quote: Keyword monitoring, detected conversations, and the overall advanced moderation destination are included in the Microsoft 365 enterprise plan.

claims.claim: The 50% threshold is an organization-level condition rather than a requirement to assign premium licenses to each communicator.
claims.quote: Other Viva Engage admin roles can also administer premium features without an assigned premium license.

claims.claim: Viva Engage admin roles other than Global and Engage administrators can administer premium features without an assigned premium license.
claims.quote: Other Viva Engage admin roles can also administer premium features without an assigned premium license.

claims.claim: No meter is documented for the permission or theme moderation as of November 2026.

claims.claim: No license specific to the moderation permission itself is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage theme moderation pricing licensing meter consumption advanced moderation permission. Read manage-data-compliance, lmc-keyword-monitoring-admin-article, eac-key-admin-roles-permissions and Viva pricing; requirements concern the moderation features, not a separate permission license.

claims.claim: Licensing is mixed, with an enterprise-plan component and a premium-license threshold for themes.
claims.quote: Theme moderation requires at least 50% of users in your organization to have the Viva Suite license, or the Viva Employee Communications and Communities license. Keyword monitoring, detected conversations, and the overall advanced moderation destination are included in the Microsoft 365 enterprise plan.

claims.claim: Theme creation and its action toggles are reached through Communications dashboard > Advanced moderation > Add theme.
claims.quote:
Go to Communications dashboard > Advanced moderation, and select Add theme.
Enter a sensible category phrase in the Theme box.
Enable the Auto-mute and Email notification toggles.

claims.claim: The theme creator chooses Auto-mute and Email notification actions while creating a theme.
claims.quote:
Add useful themes with the following steps:
1. Go to Communications dashboard > Advanced moderation, and select Add theme.
2. Enter a sensible category phrase in the Theme box.
3. Enable the Auto-mute and Email notification toggles.

claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to review and retire moderation themes is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Review the theme list against the 30-theme limit and retire themes that produce noise. | Table rows cover permission assignment, Corporate Communicator role assignment and AI Summarization, not theme management.

claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to use network export or eDiscovery is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Use network export or eDiscovery for conversations older than 30 days, which drop out of the advanced moderation pages. | No controls-table row covers network export or eDiscovery.
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout checklist bullet beginning 'Use network export or eDiscovery'; neither mechanism has a controls-table row. Keep the supported retrieval information in Risk assessment and do not add rows as part of this correction.
